panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Patient ocular ultrasonography directly demonstrates a retinal-origin hyperechoic intraocular mass with reflective posterior acoustic shadowing characteristic of retinoblastoma calcification. B: Sagittal T2-weighted MRI shows a solid intraocular mass with multiple hypointense foci identified by the caption as microcalcifications, a characteristic manifestation of retinoblastoma.

findings.label: Pineal gland tumor associated with trilateral disease
findings.evidence: Caption: "midline embryonal tumors in both the suprasellar and the pineal regions"; the figure title identifies this as trilateral retinoblastoma.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Sagittal contrast-enhanced MRI from a 2-year-old boy with hereditary bilateral retinoblastoma demonstrates the pineal and suprasellar midline tumors constituting trilateral disease. [raw subtype: trilateral retinoblastoma with midline embryonal tumors] B: The MRI directly demonstrates the pineal tumor associated with trilateral retinoblastoma in the same 2-year-old patient. [raw subtype: trilateral retinoblastoma with pineal tumor] C: Axial heavily T2-weighted MRI is explicitly captioned as revealing bilateral retinoblastoma, with arrows indicating the ocular tumors. The available vocabulary has no key for MRI demonstration of a noncalcified intraocular retinoblastoma mass. [raw subtype: bilateral retinoblastoma]

B Sagittal contrast-enhanced T1-weighted image demonstrating a pinealoblastoma (arrow). C Axial heavily T2-weighted image from the same patient revealing bilateral retinoblastoma (arrows)
in_text_mentions: dren with hereditary retinoblastoma are at risk of developing CNS embryonal tumors, histologically similar to retinoblastoma, in the pineal region or, less frequently, in the suprasellar region (Fig. 6). This presentation, known as “trilateral” retinoblastoma, carries a significantly higher mortality risk [19]. Early detection of asymptomatic pineal trilateral retinoblastoma improves survival outcomes compared to symptomatic cases of pinealoblastoma [20]. findings.label: Flexner-Wintersteiner rosettes
findings.evidence: Caption identifies Flexner-Wintersteiner rosettes in the enucleated eye of case 4.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (a, b). a: H&E photomicrograph from an enucleated human eye showing characteristic retinoblastoma histology, including Flexner-Wintersteiner and Homer Wright rosettes. [raw subtype: grade 2 differentiated retinoblastoma] b: H&E photomicrograph from the enucleated eye of case 3 showing poorly differentiated retinoblastoma with hyperchromatic small round blue cells and perivascular cuffing. [raw subtype: poorly differentiated retinoblastoma]
panels.attribution_text: Alotaibi et al. The first retinoblastoma local experience in Kuwait: A retrospective case series.. American journal of ophthalmology case reports 2024. doi:10.1016/j.ajoc.2023.101988. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: Pathology photomicrographs of the enucleated eyes of retinoblastoma cases: (a) Left eye of case 4 – it shows grade 2 retinoblastoma composed of sheets of malignant small round blue cell admixed with Flexner-Wintersteiner rosettes (white arrow) and Homer Wright rosettes (black arrow) (H&E stain, x200). Which is similar to case 1 and case 5. (b) Left eye of case 3 – it shows poorly differentiated retinoblastoma composed of malignant small round blue cell exhibiting scant cytoplasm, hyperchromatic nuclei with perivascular cuffing (H&E stain; x200). (For interpretation of the references to colour in this figure legend, the reader is referred to the Web version of this article.)
